the development and testing of an effective algorithm for stemming Slovene words, and the evaluation of its use for natural-language access to Slovene textual data.
the development of a retrieval system for Slovene textual data, and with the evaluation of the effectiveness of the system.
the effectiveness of stemming algorithms in the Slovene language.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stemming is a very effective means for conflating morphologically variant words in Slovene-language free-text retrieval systems.
stemming of Slovene documents and queries results in a statistically significant increase in retrieval effectiveness over nonconflated retrieval.
stemming is effective for Slovene, but not for English.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effectiveness of retrieval systems for Slovene language documents can be significantly increased by the use of stemming.
stemming algorithms can improve the effectiveness of natural-language information retrieval, but only for languages that have a high level of morphological complexity.
stemming algorithms should be used in natural-language retrieval systems, and that these algorithms should be designed for the language being processed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of stemming is determined by the complexity of the language.
stemming algorithms are not equally effective for all languages.
the effectiveness of the stemmer is determined by the language it is designed for.
